title: Unit Testing AI Services with xUnit & Mocking
description: Write fast, deterministic unit tests for .NET AI applications by mocking IChatClient, validating prompt templates, and testing tool dispatchers.

data.text: Unit tests must be fast (executing in milliseconds), completely deterministic (yielding the exact same assertion result on every run), and runnable in offline CI environments without requiring cloud API keys or paying token costs. In AI systems, you achieve this by isolating the deterministic application code—prompt formatting, tool parameter validation, retry logic, and JSON parsing—and mocking the underlying model abstraction (IChatClient).
Mocking IChatClient with Moq in C#
Because Microsoft.Extensions.AI standardizes the IChatClient interface, mocking a model's response Choice, token Usage, and tool-call payload in xUnit tests is clean and straightforward.

data.title: Unit Test for Ticket Triage Service with Mocked IChatClient in xUnit
data.content: Verifies classification logic without making external network calls:

data.text: Unit tests must verify that invalid tool call arguments generated by an LLM trigger meaningful validation errors and that C# tool handlers handle nulls, empty collections, and boundary numbers safely.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Unit tests must be fast, deterministic, and free of live network dependencies or API token costs
Mock Microsoft.Extensions.AI IChatClient to simulate model completions and tool invocations
Assert on the exact prompt templates and messages submitted to the model using mock verification
Test structured output deserialization and domain validation logic thoroughly with boundary inputs
Use FluentAssertions for clean, readable assertions in xUnit suites
data.takeaway: Decoupling AI logic via IChatClient makes unit testing fast, deterministic, and cost-free. Testing prompt builders and tool dispatchers with mocks ensures application logic is rock solid before deployment.
